network_boundary.actual_implementation: Both Dockerfiles start uvicorn on 0.0.0.0; EXPOSE documents container ports but does not itself publish a host port. No compose topology exists in the repository.
network_boundary.documented_exposure_risk: docs/OPERATIONS_RUNBOOK.md publishes inference with -p 8001:8001. Docker's unqualified publish binds all host interfaces by default; access from another machine then depends on host firewall/network policy.
network_boundary.safe_supported_local_topology: Host API on 127.0.0.1:8000 or a separately governed ingress; inference container published only as -p 127.0.0.1:8001:8001; API uses ATLAS_INFERENCE_SERVICE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8001; Ollama remains loopback/private at 11434.
network_boundary.safe_supported_container_topology: API and inference containers may use a private user-defined Docker bridge with no published inference port, and API may use an internal DNS/service URL at port 8001. A compose file is not supplied, so this is a supported HTTP topology rather than a repository-provided deployment artifact.

exposure_truth_table.127.0.0.1:8001: Host-local only when Docker uses -p 127.0.0.1:8001:8001 or a host process binds loopback.
exposure_truth_table.0.0.0.0:8001: Listens on all interfaces in the relevant network namespace; externally reachable when host-published/firewall-permitted.
exposure_truth_table.docker_bridge_without_publish: Reachable only by containers attached to the same bridge, not directly from the host/external network.
exposure_truth_table.host_networking: Container shares host network; an 0.0.0.0 bind is host-wide and is not an acceptable inference default without restrictive host firewall policy.
exposure_truth_table.docker_publish_8001_8001: Publishes to all host interfaces by default; unsafe for unauthenticated /generate.

inference_boundary.authorization_boundary: API only: JWT validation, token-derived tenant/user/role context, tenant-filtered retrieval, and EvidenceResolver authorization occur before prompt construction.
inference_boundary.inference_payload: Rendered evidence-grounded prompt, request_id, max_new_tokens, temperature, and optional model name. No JWT, bearer token, caller context, tenant database record, or raw retrieval set is included by the defined schema.
inference_boundary.inference_service_authentication: None; the tested contract intentionally ignores Authorization headers. Network isolation is therefore mandatory.
inference_boundary.service_to_service_auth_requirement: Not required only if private network/loopback isolation is demonstrably enforced. If that invariant cannot be enforced operationally, a separately approved service-authentication design is required before exposure.

fail_closed_behavior.tenant_or_context_mismatch: /query returns 403 before pipeline execution; verified JWT claims replace client context.
fail_closed_behavior.unavailable_inference_or_model: Readiness is false and API returns bounded 503 behavior; repeated failures are protected by the configured circuit breaker.
fail_closed_behavior.inference_timeout: Bounded timeout returns 504; queue saturation returns 429.
fail_closed_behavior.invalid_inference_response: The client validates the response schema; malformed output becomes an error and is not returned as a grounded answer. C2 validation remains after generation.
fail_closed_behavior.misconfigured_inference_url: A nonempty bad URL yields failed readiness/unavailable behavior rather than an external fallback. An empty value falls back only to loopback http://127.0.0.1:8001.

canary_compatibility.configuration_scope: The canary verifies release hashes and starts isolated loopback Ollama at 127.0.0.1:11434 with QuantizedLocalProvider. It does not start the FastAPI API or the standalone inference-service container.
canary_compatibility.assessment: Compatible with the release identities and private-loopback principle, but it does not validate the API/inference network boundary, endpoint policy, or deployment variable contract.

resource_envelope.validated_scope: single-node CPU deployment, Intel Core i3-N305 class with approximately 8 GB RAM, Gemma 3 1B Q4_K_M via Ollama, one concurrent inference, 0.5 second queue timeout, 30 second request deadline, 25 second inference-service read timeout, circuit breaker threshold 3 and 10 second cooldown
resource_envelope.not_certified: internet deployment without an approved TLS/ingress boundary, high-QPS or multi-replica operation, Kubernetes/multi-node deployment, GPU, or public inference service exposure

findings.evidence: Dockerfile.inference binds 0.0.0.0:8001, /generate has no authentication by design, and docs/OPERATIONS_RUNBOOK.md lines 255-270 use -p 8001:8001.
findings.impact: The documented command can make unauthenticated generation and its readiness endpoints host-network reachable.
findings.required_action: Approve and enforce private/loopback-only inference exposure; decide whether network isolation is the formal control or whether an approved service-authentication design is needed.

findings.evidence: src/novastack/service/resilience.py line 99 reads ATLAS_MAX_CONCURRENT_QUERIES, while docs/OPERATIONS_RUNBOOK.md line 186 and Phase 5K records state ATLAS_MAX_CONCURRENT_INFERENCES.
findings.impact: The documented value is ignored at runtime; the certified default remains 1, but an operational override silently fails.
findings.required_action: Reconcile deployment documentation and generated release-record templates to source canonical names, or approve a backwards-compatible source alias in a later controlled phase.

findings.evidence: The API reads ATLAS_INFERENCE_SERVICE_URL for port 8001; InferenceServiceConfig reads ATLAS_INFERENCE_BACKEND_URL for Ollama, normally port 11434. Phase 5K material uses BACKEND_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8001.
findings.impact: A copied historical configuration can point the wrong component at the wrong service.
findings.required_action: Publish a single current configuration table and preserve historical manifests as immutable provenance; do not edit certified artifact records.

findings.evidence: The API defines no route-level access restriction for /healthz, /ready, or /metrics; existing runbook treats them as directly curlable.
findings.impact: Operational state may be exposed if API port 8000 is broadly published.
findings.required_action: Document ingress/firewall policy: /query authenticated user-facing only; health, readiness, and metrics local/private/operator-only.

findings.evidence: docs/ATLAS_0.5_ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW.md line 198 and historical scripts use ATLAS_JWT_*; runtime reads only ATLAS_AUTH_*.
findings.impact: Operators could supply inert names and obtain a fail-closed unconfigured API.
findings.required_action: Mark ATLAS_JWT_* as historical/inert in active operator material.

required_changes: Security governance decision for the inference network boundary before any deployment using the current runbook command.
Documentation-only reconciliation of active runbook/configuration guidance; exact drift locations are recorded in OPS-01 findings.
No production source change was made or automatically authorized by OPS-01. A future service-authentication change requires separate design approval if private-network enforcement is not assured.
